implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is a gating checkpoint in Indian takeover law: once a party acquires shares crossing specified thresholds (typically 5% and thereafter every 2%), public disclosure becomes mandatory and stops information asymmetry, directly impacting share price and derivative litigation risk for target and acquirer.

headline: Punjab Produce & Trading Co. Pvt. Ltd. files substantial acquisition disclosure for Birla Corporation Limited
sum: **Punjab Produce & Trading Co. Pvt. Ltd. has filed a disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations Regulation 31(4)** regarding substantial acquisition of shares in listed company Birla Corporation Limited, triggering mandatory public disclosure obligations under the takeover code.
detail: The disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 was filed by Punjab Produce & Trading Co. Pvt. Ltd. with the NSE. This disclosure mechanism ensures that significant shareholding changes in listed companies are immediately communicated to stock exchanges and the public. The specific acquisition details—including number of shares, consideration, and acquirer intent—would be contained in the formal disclosure document filed with the exchange.
